claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily focused on gathering resources and crafting rather than traditional action role-playing mechanics.

citations.review_text: I thought this would be a traditional ARPG, a Diablo clone, if I'm being reductive. What I got instead was a crafting/survival game, with some ARPG elements sprinkled throughout. I found that many mechanics were poorly explained or not explained at all. From what I understand, many people enjoy having a Wiki page open on a second screen while gaming, but I am not one of them. My biggest takeaway from this game is that it wasn't for me!

This game seemed like  alot of fun judging from the store page videos, but when I got to play it that wasnt the case.

 You are a vampire that gather wood and rocks to make a sawmill and other things, not what I was looking for.

it feels weird to hop into a game that's supposed to be about being a vampire growing in power and placing yourself above all the mortal cattle and the first thing you're doing is slowly, dully, repeatedly chipping away at trees and rocks to do typical video game crafting nonsense

Short; Boring grindfest, no story other than intro 'cutscene' thought it'd be a drastically different game, not just a top down rust with a vampire aesthetic. 

Long; Had my eyes on this game for a while and tried during the current free weekend, I was severely disappointed, the game seems at conflict with itself.
Price is rather steep, for the quality especially, 35 USD for a lackluster game, along with 100 USD 'DLC' aka cosmetics. seems the focus is more on getting money than adding flushed out systems.
In terms of combat/gameplay it could have dealt with a better premise. it is strictly an online game, along with the fun 'play our game or you could lost progress' now with an option for even more progress lost! it plays like Diablo/PoE but with a less satisfying feel and even less scaling. no skills or levels, just a gear system that arguably doesn't matter.
Story is very non-existent, it lives strictly in the opening, *spoilers* the story is rather short, vampires strong, human attack, vampires weak, you vampire, go beat up skeletons to escape.


If you enjoy grindfests you *Might* enjoy the game but I sincerely cannot recommend it as a fan of Vampires or video games themselves.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that movement speed is very slow and requires walking long distances across the map.

citations.review_text:
Cool concept, poor execution. 

The movement speed is so slow for a map this size, I have to walk for nearly 5 minutes to get to my body in the starting zone, after dying repeatedly to a boss that, according to the game's quest system, I should be able to beat. The combat also felt pretty clunky.

My base despawned after the first time I played, my own fault but still frustrating. I got a housing plot in the starting area, but a spider twice my level kept spawning in it and killing me while I was just trying to build my base and progress.

A grindy survival and base builder game with vampire elements.

With some gameplay polish and more story content the game could be a lot better.
Now it is neither bad nor good. Just so-so.
Get it on sale in case you are vampire fan and wanna build your own castle while hunting around.

+ + + Graphics are nice.
+ + + Online version adds some life to the map. (But note there are not much server with people.)
+ + + During daylight you must hide in shadows otherwise will burn to crisps. This adds some variety to the gameplay.

- - - Combat sytem is not really good. Base attack spam with some dodge. Camera angles can trick you. Blood sucking animation is strange for me.
- - - Too much grind required to progress.
- - - Running is way too slow, horse riding is somewhat better.
- - - No story at all apart from the intro video. Such a BIG MISSED OPPORTUNITY.

citations.review_text: I thought this would be a traditional ARPG, a Diablo clone, if I'm being reductive. What I got instead was a crafting/survival game, with some ARPG elements sprinkled throughout. I found that many mechanics were poorly explained or not explained at all. From what I understand, many people enjoy having a Wiki page open on a second screen while gaming, but I am not one of them. My biggest takeaway from this game is that it wasn't for me!

Tried during the free weekend and got 90 mins out of it before I just gave up. 

I must have died about a dozen times before I even got around to build my castle, which I never even did cause I couldn't be bothered anymore and I couldn't find out how to place floors as the game doesn't tell you.

The sun WILL kill you, everything WILL kill you, usually within a few shots. - You get overwhelmed by enemies.. You MUST hide during daylight hours and you can't get drawn into fights as you will die, 100% of the time from sun exposure and enemies. 

There's 7 hours of daylight which probably converts into about 5-8 mins of just literally standing in the shade, moving occasionally when the sun moves the shade.

You cannot pause the game either, big mistake by the devs there. - If you pause the game you will die from something finding you and attacking you, this is 2026 and you can't pause a game? - bollocks.

The difficulty is ridiculous, even on "relaxed" mode.

Don't get me wrong, I do love a challenge, I play WARHAMMER 40k: Space Marine 2,  on the highest difficulty you can set it too. 

But there's a MASSIVE difference between a "Satisfying challenge" or a "Frustrating challenge". - and V rising sits firmly in the "Frustrating challenge"

So I have to have a cool down on my abilities while my enemies don't? - I have to fight half a dozen enemies all at once, when I'm already weak as hell? - Dying all the time in, which is essentially the tutorial bit is infuriating. - at least, you know, let me build my castle at first before you send 100 people my way to try and kill me.

I have to constantly maintain my castle or I lose it? - That seems about the only fair bit of the game so far.

Every time I die, I lose all my resources but I can go grab them back again but this means having to travel the map to get them every single time. - which means I have to fight the same enemies over and over and then hide again, over and over when the sun comes out.

I do like the game thoug…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the camera controls on a controller require holding down a trigger to freely rotate the view.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to enjoy V Rising because the game itself has a lot going for it. The visuals, combat, progression, and survival mechanics are all excellent. Unfortunately, the controller implementation completely overshadowed those strengths for me.

My biggest issue is the camera controls. The default controller scheme requires continuously holding L2 to freely rotate the camera. I don't mind isometric games at all, I actually enjoy them, but this is one of the most uncomfortable controller schemes I've experienced. Constantly holding a trigger while moving, fighting, dodging, and managing abilities quickly became frustrating and unnecessarily fatiguing.

Before deciding to leave this review, I spent a good amount of time trying to solve the problem with Steam Input. I tested custom configurations and community layouts, expecting to remap the controls into something that felt more natural. None of them achieved the result I was looking for. From my experience, the game's controller implementation limits what Steam Input can do with the camera controls, leaving the default behavior essentially unchanged.

This isn't a complaint from someone who gave up after a few minutes. I genuinely wanted to make the game work on controller and invested the time trying to fix what I considered its biggest flaw. Unfortunately, after exhausting every solution I could find, I came to the conclusion that this is simply how the controller support is designed.

For me, the camera controls were a major drawback that prevented me from enjoying an otherwise excellent game. If the developers ever add native options for more conventional camera controls or allow greater customization, I'd gladly revisit my recommendation.

Until then, I can't recommend V Rising based on my experience as a controller first player.
Camera angle is so bad, makes it unplayable.

cohorts.summary: Players navigate punishing sunlight mechanics and restriction on teleporting items.

claims.claim: Teleportation waypoints cannot be used while carrying certain items such as ores in the inventory, requiring players to walk across the map.

citations.review_text:
Starts off interesting but quickly devolves into a long, boring grindfest. 
Did you just grind for an hour to unlock a new item?
Congrats! Now you have to grind to unlock the materials needed to craft your reward!
Did you gather a bunch of materials? Sorry, but you can't teleport now. You'll have to backtrack across the entire map every time you go out. 

I'm baffled as to how this game has positive reviews.
You mf's must not have jobs or something.

What starts as something that looks to be very fun devolves into a frustration filled grind. Waypoints/Teleports that become inaccessible the second you're holding inventory, Waiting 5 minutes to grind bricks to put a single wall up when you need at least 20 to fit. The entire experience just becomes more frustration dealing with a near instakill daytime mechanic. More trouble than its worth to where I wish I'd gotten a refund rather than trying to power through what I thought was a rough spot and ended up just being the gameplay loop.

Hello gamer friends,

I played the game for free on Solo because that is my preferred play style. V Rising does not have a traditional story mode. While it features some lore and character biographies, the game is primarily a sandbox survival RPG where players create their own story through gameplay choices and interactions with NPCs. There are no main quests or significant narrative-driven storylines, but we can engage with other players online if that is something anyone here reading is interested in.
I liked some of the features like jumping from ledges, transforming into animals and even some of the skills that were almost similar to a necromancer. Besides the jumping from ledges function, there was no fun way to traverse the map in a convenient way. Slow movement/running, no legit fast travel unless you basically drop all important items from your inventory first. Also, Tracking was strange because some targets would be trackable while two never allowed me to track them even after selecting the target and it giving the impression I was tracking the target. (Maybe a bug?)
Now me personally, I was hoping there was a story mode that allowed me to understand my character's background and maybe give meaningful tasks that contributed to understanding my characters reasoning for becoming a vampire, contribute to the overall story along with gaining permanent unique NPCs as I progressed the story but this was not the case. Nothing gave me a sense of motivation or fulfillment for any of the randomness of various tasks in-game. The main point of the of the game was to track targets, defeat targets, consume targets. While I knocked out mostly all the ACTs before the free play availability was over, I gave up on chasing down targets and focused on building my castle. This part was the most fun, especially after dominating and turning NPCs into minions. I spent so many hours building the perfect castle that I no longer cared to venture further to uncharted areas on the map.…

claims.claim: The sun mechanic damages or kills the player during daytime, forcing players to hide in shadows or inside bases.

citations.review_text: V Rising has got to be the most boring vampire game ever made. You get to play the world's slowest vampire who is weaker than a malnourished child, killing endlessly respawning MOBA minions patrolling a randomly generated world map with a generic primary attack for scraps of trash used to build a castle and upgrade gear. Except everything is maxed out in the first hour and the rest of the upgrades seem to be locked behind bosses that you have to somehow kill with your anemic excuse of a vampire who can't run, roll, dodge, or even block attacks, except for dash and parry spells that are both on a cooldown. The character is so slow you can't even get out of area of effect attacks unless you have the dash spell primed. As a result, fights turn into slow, deliberate slogs of perfectly timed attacks and parries, while manually rotating the camera to keep the character and the boss in view. Sure, you can keep grinding to unlock more spells and abilities, making the character faster and stronger, but to what end?  So you can grind some more? The game is just fundamentally not fun to play. Oh, and you can't even sleep through the day, so half the time you are crouched in the shadow of a tree somewhere, waiting for the sun to go down so you can keep going. Sounds fun, doesn't it?

Wonderful cute game :) you get to make your vampire castle and feel really cool
Careful of the sun tho :P nasty sunlight burns you

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features engaging, gothic-themed visuals and castle building.

citations.review_text:
[b]🏰  I Became Vampire King!! 🏰 [/b]

V Rising perfectly captures the atmosphere of a dark, gothic, vampire-infested world. From gorgeous art direction to distinct zone color palettes, the visual design is stunning. It is essentially a compact, Diablo-style action RPG mixed with phenomenal base building.

Dynamic Progression: 
No traditional levels or XP. Progression is tied directly to boss kills, forcing you to master mechanics rather than over-level by grinding.

Awesome Castle Customization:
Base building is surprisingly addictive. The gorgeous artwork naturally motivates you to pause your journey, remodel, and spend hours designing a fancy vampire estate.

Flexible Difficulty Sliders: While the raw item grind can be tedious, developer-provided resource drop sliders let you skip the farming and save time so you can enjoy the other activities.

Challenging Boss Design: 
Boss encounters are tough, creative, and mechanically deep. Some acts act as real skill checks, requiring tactical re-specing and community build guides to crack.

Slow Traversal: 
Early-game foot travel feels sluggish. Horses feel unlocked a bit too late, and the game-changing Bat Form arrives at the absolute endgame.

Linear Structure:
Because everything unlocks via specific bosses, the game progression can feel a bit linear and limited. You dont have much choice here. You follow the predefined path.

Vague Story:
The lore is barely there. A few Elden Ring-style NPCs with cryptic dialogue would have made the world feel much more impactful.

[b] Summary: 8/10 [b/]
If you are on the fence, wishlist it and wait for a sale. Snagging this for $15–$20 is an absolute bargain for a long weekend of gaming. Highly recommended!

Everything in this game feels good, the battle mechanics, the bossing, the management, the survival & the vibes. It's really cool being a vampire, avoiding the sun & all. LOVE the Victorian gothic themes.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a music box for the castle and includes the Castlevania song Bloody Tears from the DLC.

citations.review_text:
TL;DR Good music (love the music box for the castle), nice graphics, fun combat, stupid and annoying death mechanic (lose inventory), customisable solo PvE server creation, cheat commands that can make it more fun for some. Overall, a pretty good game.

Just beat the game a little while ago, without any of the cool DLC decorations /sadface. so, yeah. I played on a customised solo PvE server on super easy-ish because it was fun for me. I've always thought having to run back to where you died to get your dropped inventory is an incredibly stupid mechanic, but, thankfully, this game has cheat commands that made the game fun for me. I played with invulnerability on, which obviously makes things easier since you don't have to worry about dying (you can lose your blood, though), but the fights still take time and strategy (if you want to try to avoid stuns and all that) so it's not like it was a mindless cakewalk. Being able to Ctrl+Shift+click to teleport is awesome and I teleported myself into some weird places several times (one where I actual vanished, and so did everything on my quickbars, after I accidentally teleported into a tree outside my castle); other times, I teleported right next to a V Blood, tracked and otherwise, by happy accident.

The music for the base game is pretty cool and I had them all on shuffle inside my castle (love that they have a music box for us). The graphics are pretty good and the base game castle decorations are nice. The combat has limited skills/animations, but I thought it was fun. The thrones and soul shard storage being too tall for one floor sucks, would be nice if that could have been updated when they added more floors to castles (maybe make each floor taller). I didn't know about this and my castle wasn't built to accommodate them so they're shoved in a corner where I guess I didn't build out the second floor balcony.  I'm sure I have more to say, but this is already too long so, bye.

I claimed the key from a giveaway in 2023 …

This game is super fun, especially in co-op with friends. The combat is difficult enough (currently playing on the hardest difficulty) to be challenging and fun. The number of unique enemy units is perfect to keep you from learning a few move sets and then beating everything.

The base building is entertaining. I love seeing what I can make with each castle upgrade.

The music in the game is very good, especially the Castlevania song, Bloody Tears, from the DLC. I listen to that on repeat.

The atmosphere, ambience, and environment of the game is well-thought out. It's a beautiful game.

Highly recommended.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the progression as strictly tied to defeating bosses rather than traditional leveling.

citations.review_text:
Game starts out great, but quickly becomes a MASSIVE grindfest as you get towards the end.

+ combat is fun
+ cool builds
+ all abilities useful

+/- No levels by themselves. You level by crafting better armor. Think Monster hunter.
+/- Game is a boss run.

- Grind fest
- No story whatsoever.
- Game can be played solo but it's definitely meant for more than 1 player.
- Durability. Why do devs add durability to armor and weapons and everything else. Get rid of it, or give us an option to disable it. When you die to a boss, you take a big durability hit. Once your armor/weapon breaks, you drop in level (see below). Dropping in level in this game is HUGE. It's bad if it's mid-boss fight.
- Towards the endgame, armor breaks, and the materials to fix it are what create all the grinding you have to do to repair your gear. Very annoying.
- The sun is an interesting concept, but it's absolutely stupid to put in a game like this. And you cannot turn it off. Best you can do is turn down its timer. The sun itself will make or break an entire fight. I do not understand why devs didn't give us the option to just disable it entirely. Playing on the hardest difficulty makes this so much more annoying.
 
I get the positive reviews. I want to recommend it. But I can't because of these annoying things that should've been dumped when the game was in early access. If these things ever get fixed and I get notified, I will change my review to a thumbs up without hesitation, as the bosses are very fun and unique to fight, albeit, some very annoying to fight too. This can be overlooked. The other issues cannot.

V Rising is sort of a finished game. As in, there is sort of progression with sort of endgame with sort of gameplay loop. Up to Gear Level 85ish the game is very solid but then transforms into an utter slog of farming Rifts, rolling secondary bonuses on gems, rolling secondary attributes on legendary weapons. Rift farming feels genuinely soulless, like farming in MMO but without all the things making it fun. Luckily, there are means to modify droprates/vendor prices within in-game settings, but as a game creator, your line of defense should never be "there is a button to skip the part that isn't fun".

And mentioning soulless mechanics – servants. They provide no meaningful value to the experience. You catch them, give them gear, and then send them on literal mobile game expeditions. You can’t assign them any meaningful activity. They can’t patrol regions. You can’t take them as your combat companions. You can’t even encounter them in places where you send them to. Half of Vampire appeal is being able to mind control people and create thralls, yet the mechanic is basically non-existent outside of underbaked resource generator. 

Speaking of dominating people, the other use is keeping prisoners in cages to extract blood from them. For as essential to endgame as “100% Bloods” are, getting them is pain in the back. You either encounter them naturally or play Corrupted Fish minigame where you throw anywhere from one to a few dozens of fish at your prison and see it roll random outcomes until eventually you get 100% Blood. Yet another needless grindy part. Once again, "you can just turn off the part that isn't fun" shouldn't be a line of defense for game designers.

The game itself is made with being PVP experience in mind. All the skills, cooldowns, and movement are balanced around players duking it out. Those of you who are familiar with isometric action games may get a heart attack hearing that the base cooldown of dash is 8 seconds. The game tries to compensate for t…

claims.claim: Playing on private co-op servers requires managing real-world time gating mechanisms, such as long crafting or conversion timers.

citations.review_text: I really loved the vampire theme in V Rising. Watching your humble starting base slowly evolve into a massive, grand vampire castle is incredibly satisfying, and the boss rush-style progression is highly engaging. However, playing on a private server with just friends brings up a huge issue: the real-world time mechanics. Processes like converting human servants take actual hours to complete. Even if you tweak the custom server settings to minimize these timers, it still takes way too long for a private server that isn't running 24/7. It's a great game, but this real-time gating really hurts the private co-op experience.

Really fun for online co-op, it feels pretty balanced but there are things we miss out on or don't utilize because we aren't doing PvP. I could definitely see how some of the mechanics might make playing on an online server without daily login pretty difficult, and potentially frustrating (castle heart blood drain, for example). So, I do recommend this game, but specifically for a co-op group with friends. I cannot speak for the other gameplay styles.

claims.claim: Players lose a significant portion of their equipped gear durability upon dying to bosses, which impacts character level and requires repair materials.

citations.review_text:
Game starts out great, but quickly becomes a MASSIVE grindfest as you get towards the end.

+ combat is fun
+ cool builds
+ all abilities useful

+/- No levels by themselves. You level by crafting better armor. Think Monster hunter.
+/- Game is a boss run.

- Grind fest
- No story whatsoever.
- Game can be played solo but it's definitely meant for more than 1 player.
- Durability. Why do devs add durability to armor and weapons and everything else. Get rid of it, or give us an option to disable it. When you die to a boss, you take a big durability hit. Once your armor/weapon breaks, you drop in level (see below). Dropping in level in this game is HUGE. It's bad if it's mid-boss fight.
- Towards the endgame, armor breaks, and the materials to fix it are what create all the grinding you have to do to repair your gear. Very annoying.
- The sun is an interesting concept, but it's absolutely stupid to put in a game like this. And you cannot turn it off. Best you can do is turn down its timer. The sun itself will make or break an entire fight. I do not understand why devs didn't give us the option to just disable it entirely. Playing on the hardest difficulty makes this so much more annoying.
 
I get the positive reviews. I want to recommend it. But I can't because of these annoying things that should've been dumped when the game was in early access. If these things ever get fixed and I get notified, I will change my review to a thumbs up without hesitation, as the bosses are very fun and unique to fight, albeit, some very annoying to fight too. This can be overlooked. The other issues cannot.

TL;DR Good music (love the music box for the castle), nice graphics, fun combat, stupid and annoying death mechanic (lose inventory), customisable solo PvE server creation, cheat commands that can make it more fun for some. Overall, a pretty good game.

Just beat the game a little while ago, without any of the cool DLC decorations /sadface. so, yeah. I played on a customised solo PvE server on super easy-ish because it was fun for me. I've always thought having to run back to where you died to get your dropped inventory is an incredibly stupid mechanic, but, thankfully, this game has cheat commands that made the game fun for me. I played with invulnerability on, which obviously makes things easier since you don't have to worry about dying (you can lose your blood, though), but the fights still take time and strategy (if you want to try to avoid stuns and all that) so it's not like it was a mindless cakewalk. Being able to Ctrl+Shift+click to teleport is awesome and I teleported myself into some weird places several times (one where I actual vanished, and so did everything on my quickbars, after I accidentally teleported into a tree outside my castle); other times, I teleported right next to a V Blood, tracked and otherwise, by happy accident.

The music for the base game is pretty cool and I had them all on shuffle inside my castle (love that they have a music box for us). The graphics are pretty good and the base game castle decorations are nice. The combat has limited skills/animations, but I thought it was fun. The thrones and soul shard storage being too tall for one floor sucks, would be nice if that could have been updated when they added more floors to castles (maybe make each floor taller). I didn't know about this and my castle wasn't built to accommodate them so they're shoved in a corner where I guess I didn't build out the second floor balcony.  I'm sure I have more to say, but this is already too long so, bye.

I claimed the key from a giveaway in 2023 …

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game lacks an official server support or offline solo save structure that does not require an active connection.

citations.review_text:
Every aspect of this game is at least good. I especially love music. However, I can't recommend this game for it has a gigantic IF for me- server connection. Some will think that i have thrash internet. Well I have never complained in any multiplayer game (Terraria, LoL, Overwatch, Minecraft, GTA V etc.) about stability and ping but in V Rising I unfortunetly have. 

First time i launched the game there was a server's region to choose, i did chose mine. Then I started playing SOLO. Guess what, I have had lags. I launched the game in LAN mode- still lags. Game is really enjoyable so i played but the more I progressed and enemies became more difficult the more frustrated I was. Imagine fighting boss when you barely lost any health, then one lag starts for 2-6 seconds, alert on screen says u lost connection to server then lag passes just for you to find that you are dead. And those 2-6 sec lags happens at least once every 10 sec of gameplay or so. Then you fight this boss again and again and you wait for a fight when u have lags as short as possible just to defeat it by luck and repetition, not by skill. Insufferable experience.

It is beyond me that in 2026 a game that has dedicated payed servers can't run a solo offline save for a player. There is no reason for connection anyways if i don't use any community related function. Aside offline solo "servers", why game with various server regions has such problems with stable connection in Europe. We are not speaking about some distant, remote place so how come!?
its fun but why is there no official server support?

Great game. It is unapologetically vampire, edgy, gothic and more. - starts off quite slow as all survival games do but this game evolves to be a very fun ARPG style game. 

The building is great and though a little clunky at times, you are given a wide array of decoration pieces and aesthetics you may follow. You are also encouraged to create rooms which I quite liked.

I recommend playing on Brutal if you only intend to play through once as bosses gain new, challenging mechanics. I also suggest to adjust loot gain and crafting speed accordingly based on your player count. You do not want to sit at standard 1x rules when you are playing with one other person.

Difficulty is a little all over the place in terms of boss design, but I think overall from a PvE, low player count perspective they are mostly fun. 

It is very frustrating (naturally so) on ping but we still managed to clear it moderately easily, struggling only on a couple of bosses. 

Overall great stuff, just needs some minor tweaking from the host based on your player count.

citations.review_text: Combat is a lot of fun, and I like the base building. Although the resource gathering is grindy as hell but I think you can adjust it. You can definitely tell this is leaning towards a multiplayer PvPvE type of game (still a lot of fun solo)
An amazing game but somewhat grindy. However, there are in game settings that help alleviate the grind.

just a fun progressive game where you rp as a vampire. i'd recommend jimmying the settings though to make farming abit quicker and nicer. give yourself more minions if you don't expect to play in large stints.

[b] Change the settings to fit around your playstyle. [/b] There is no need for a casual playthrough to have long crafting times or for items to restrict teleporting if its going to negatively affect your experience. PVP servers can use these to force player interaction and keep risk involved. 

Bored of grinding resources? Increase the resource yield.
Tired of waiting for [spoiler] Rift Incursions? [/spoiler] Increase the frequency and decrease the wait.
Tired of spending all of your time avoiding the sun? Tweak the day/night cycle times.
[b] Spend your time enjoying the game. [/b]

The combat is unique to quite a few of the boss & crafting based progression games I have played and it scratches the itch juggling both defensive and offensive abilities and strategies. Multiplayer elevates this allowing for harder and easier fights depending on your teams experience level & brutal difficulty adds so much depth to the boss fights with new mechanics forcing you to use everything at your disposal.

The base building and crafting gives a ton of freedom but it also has its flaws. As you play you will continue to unlock more ways of crafting and upgrades to your current crafting stations changing their sizes and shapes requiring constant reorganization. If you build a multi-level base or need to move your base prepare for difficulty. With it being a fairly grind intensive game you will probably get the most enjoyment out of building your ideal base the first time, with subsequent playthroughs feeling more tiresome.

Overall I'd highly recommend it to anyone who is interested (especially for the combat!), but multiplayer is much more enjoyable. There's a TON to explore and even more to do and its much more manageable with at least one other person.

Well polished. Satisfying progression. You have the freedom to make many unique character builds. Fun and engaging castle management. One of the best building systems I've ever played. Bosses have new/additional game mechanics on higher difficulties. This will forever be in the list of my all-time top games.

I was not expecting to be into this game and I could not be more pleasantly surprised. This game was an excellent all around gaming experience. Good balanced progression with interesting boss mechanics all the way through. It also wrapped up very nicely as a complete game. Fantastic multiplayer aspects with or without pvp. And it was also stunningly beautiful. Absolutely loved the castle building and decorating. The lore was interesting and it had easter eggs. The boss fights were very challenging, immersive and sometimes hilarious. It was challenging but not too punishing, but also adjustable in the settings if you wanted more difficulty. I really couldn't recommend it enough.

If you love base building and the fantasy of being a full‑power, night‑dwelling vampire, V Rising absolutely delivers. The progression system is one of the best parts of the game — no boring XP grind, no endless leveling treadmill. You get stronger by earning better gear, hunting bosses, drinking their V‑blood, and unlocking new powers and crafting stations. It feels clean, rewarding, and genuinely addictive.

The castle building is top‑tier. Your base doesn’t just look cool — it feels like a real extension of your vampiric identity. Every upgrade, every new room, every servant you command adds to that sense of rising power.

Combat is fast, stylish, and surprisingly deep. The world is atmospheric and fun to explore. And the loop of hunt → craft → upgrade → dominate stays satisfying for a long time.

My only real wish is more content. The foundation is so strong that the game practically begs for more regions, bosses, spells, and castle pieces. It’s already great — it could be legendary with more updates.

I originally picked up V Rising because the idea of combining survival mechanics with Hack and Slash combat sounded interesting, and it turned out to be one of the biggest positive surprises I've had in the genre. I played most of it solo, but I also spent a good amount of time in co-op with a friend. Both ways of playing are enjoyable, although the experience feels slightly different depending on whether you're building your vampire empire alone or with someone else.

The combat is easily one of the game's strongest aspects. It has a fast pace, responsive controls, and a wide variety of weapons, spells, and abilities that encourage experimenting with different playstyles. Boss fights are particularly enjoyable. Every V Blood boss introduces unique mechanics and rewards you with new powers, recipes, or crafting stations, making progression feel meaningful instead of simply increasing your numbers.

The survival mechanics never felt overwhelming to me. You still need to gather resources, refine materials, and manage your equipment, but the game keeps introducing new tools and upgrades that make the grind feel rewarding. Rather than surviving just for the sake of surviving, you're constantly working toward expanding your vampire castle and unlocking new technologies.

Castle building deserves special praise. It's surprisingly deep and gives you a lot of freedom to create a home that not only looks good but also serves practical purposes. Organizing crafting stations, decorating rooms, and gradually transforming a small fortress into a massive vampire castle became one of my favorite parts of the game.

Exploration is also handled very well. Every new region introduces stronger enemies, different resources, and increasingly difficult bosses. Because progression is tied to defeating specific enemies, exploring the world always has a purpose. I rarely felt like I was wandering around without a goal.

citations.review_text: the best survival game in its genre, the game really surprised me there is a lot to do, the map is huge, there are too many factions that fight each other, there are lots of bosses to beat, most of them have mechanics that need to be countered or prepared for, there are a lot of weapons to choose from with different abilities, you can build your base wherever you want, there are a lot of decoration pieces to choose from, lots of slaves to catch, super good game for its price, i recommend it. 10/10

Favorite survivalcraft game.
I love the world so much. Most of the time whenever I play these kinds of games, the world feels so empty or dead but populated solely for the player. 
I love how villagers can either freeze in fear or try to square up against you.
I love how patrols of opposing factions other than your own will fight each other in the streets.
I love how you can find workers tinkering with lightning harvester towers.
Very minor stuff but they added so much life into a world and I hope other games see this and do the same.

Combat is so fun. Top down but camera can be somewhat-freely moved. I've put several hours into games like Diablo, Final Fantasy XIV, and Lost Ark, and this games grabs those and makes a survivalcraft out of them. As a melee player, I went back and forth between blood, unholy, and static, then ended up going full-on blood for the theming. 
Boss fights are so much fun! My only advise is to google on how to increase their HP pools, so that you don't kill them as fast. Or just play on Brutal difficulty! There's a few settings you can't tweak in game but can via their json files.

Builds are fun, you can mix or match. I've avoided searching meta guides like I usually do when it comes to action games, so I can't say I have mathematical experience on testing builds, but it's really nice to be able to mix and match builds and still do well. I've beaten the final boss with pure blood build, hybrid blood/necro, and hybrid blood/static. (I just really love builds that match the blood theme). It's definitely harder as a melee but it's not impossible!

Castle.......my beloved. Tile based (like huge tiles, not 1x1 size that you might be used to) and the games' machines/facilities push you to try and make separate rooms for different kinds of facilities to get bonuses like faster craft rates and cheaper craft costs. You can make several floors and mid to late game ish the game gives you in-castle teleporters so that you can get to your …

Vampires PvP, and a beautifully made combat system so smooth it goes down your throat like water. 

You want it and you know it. If you're strong enough that is :)

Probably one of the most well rounded games i have ever played. It features fluid combat, and rewards combos as well as accuracy. The solo exp is also fun good boss battles, base optimization, farming, and exploration. For me though the pvp alone is the attraction. Not only does it feature pvp but its in world not another que or lobby the same server you grind for resources etc. just like Rust the game also features a raid mechanic that is so well thought out perfect for anyone that itches for blood and glory. The farming can get a little tedious but highly rewarding and with servers that limit groups it can be balanced for the race of higher tech on wipe day. 100/10 always will be installed.

[h1]V Rising: A Gothic Masterpiece of Survival and Action Combat[/h1]

[i]V Rising is a phenomenal achievement in the survival genre, masterfully blending top-down action-RPG combat with deep base building and vampire lore. Developed by Stunlock Studios, this game successfully avoids the typical survival pitfalls by making you feel like a powerful predator reclaiming your empire, rather than just another weakling trying to stay alive. With its fluid mechanics, rich atmosphere, and highly rewarding progression, it stands as an absolute must-play for fans of both survival games and action RPGs alike.[/i]

[h2]🧛 The Vampire Power Fantasy and Atmosphere[/h2]
The atmosphere in V Rising is brilliantly dark and gothic. From the sun-dappled forests to the grim, foggy farmlands and cursed woods, the world feels incredibly alive and dangerous. What makes the game truly stand out is how it forces you to adapt to being a vampire: the sun is your absolute enemy, and navigating the shadows during the daytime turns simple travel into a tense, thrilling puzzle. The visual style is crisp and stylized, perfectly capturing the moody, blood-soaked aesthetic of a dark fantasy realm.

[h2]⚔️ Combat and Blood Types[/h2]
Combat is heavily inspired by Stunlock's previous arena-shooter pedigree, meaning it is fast, fluid, and completely skill-based. Utilizing a mix of directional skill-shots, dashes, and weapon abilities, every encounter feels incredibly engaging. The "Blood Type" system is a stroke of pure genius. Feeding on different targets—like a rogue, a brute, or a worker—grants you unique, dynamic buffs based on the quality of their blood. This turns hunting into a strategic choice, as you actively scout for the perfect prey to boost your specific playstyle.
